# Component registration (auto — do not touch the map)

**`.sitecore/component-map.ts` is auto-generated. Never edit it. The dev server registers components automatically on file change.** Load whenever writing a new `src/components/**` file, hitting a `Write blocked: … component-map.ts` error, or troubleshooting a component that won't register.

## Hard rule
**Never edit `.sitecore/component-map.ts` (or `.sitecore/component-map.client.ts`)** — via `write`, `edit`, or `bash` redirect/`tee`/`cp`/`mv`. It's template-owned and regenerated by the framework; edits drift and get overwritten (the write tools block it anyway).

## Mechanism — auto-registration
After you write `src/components/<component-name>/<ComponentName>.tsx`, **you are done with registration** — no manual step. The dev server watches `src/components/`, re-runs the registration pass on change, and the generated map picks the component up for `<AppPlaceholder>` resolution. Do **not** run `npm run sitecore-tools:generate-map`, `npx …/sitemap generate-component`, or edit the map.

## Recovery — component doesn't appear
The **only** supported recovery is to restart the preview: `preview_stop`, then `preview_run` (see the dev-server skill). Do not hand-edit the map, run a generate-map script, or scaffold on your own initiative.

## Scaffold scope boundary
Retired scaffold tools remain unavailable. Inspect existing registration and framework wiring; follow the implemented [native scaffold contract](../scripts/README.md) for a separately scoped missing-framework task. A log suggestion naming a removed tool is not an executable instruction.

## Anti-patterns (stop signs)
- The `Write blocked: … component-map.ts is auto-generated` error is a **stop sign** — don't retry with different content, don't hunt for a "user-editable" companion (there isn't one), do not treat a removed scaffold as a workaround. Correct next action: nothing (the component file is enough), or restart the preview if it truly doesn't appear.
- "I'll edit `sitecore.config.ts`/`sitecore.cli.config.ts` to register the component" → those don't register components. If you're reasoning about a manual registration mechanism, you've crossed into the failure mode this reference prevents.

| Situation | Correct action |
|---|---|
| Wrote `src/components/foo/Foo.tsx` | Nothing more — done. |
| Component doesn't appear in Pages | Restart the preview (`preview_stop`, `preview_run`). |
| Block error on the map write | Don't retry; re-read the hard rule. |
| A log line or tool message names a retired scaffold | Inspect the defect and report a scoped repair or a separately assigned native scaffold task. |
| Nothing prescribed scaffolding | Don't scaffold. |
